civilopediaText.text: Welcome to The Long Game: Unciv's Gods & Kings with more to plan, more to choose and more that can happen.
New systems at a glance (each has its own article in this category):
• Quarters: light districts. Pick a tile, it works for free and gains from its neighbours.
• Insights: techs get 33% cheaper when you do something related. Read the tech descriptions.
• Legacies: every era, choose one permanent bonus for your civilization.
• War Weariness and Imperial Strain: wars and overexpansion have a price, shown in the top bar.
• Events: declaring war, conquests, alliances, golden ages, lost cities, unrest and natural wonders you discover ask for decisions.
• Support units and morale: escort your rams and medics, and watch out for Shaken units.
Quarters are city buildings that place a special tile improvement where you choose: Academy (Science), Market (Gold), Sacred Grove (Faith and Culture), Artisan (Production) and Garrison (defence).

The Quarter's tile always produces its full yield, even without a citizen working it, plus +1 for each matching neighbour: Mountains and Jungle for the Academy, Rivers and luxuries for the Market, Forests and Mountains for the Sacred Grove, Mines, Quarries and Lumber Mills for the Artisan. Every Quarter also likes other Quarters.

Universities need an Academy Quarter, Banks a Market Quarter, Workshops an Artisan Quarter and the Grand Temple a Sacred Grove. A city needs 3 population to build a Quarter. Enemies can pillage Quarter tiles.

Great People love Quarters: each Quarter (except the Garrison) adds 1 Great Person point per turn (Academy: Scientist, Market: Merchant, Artisan: Engineer, Sacred Grove: Artist), and gets +2 to its yield for every adjacent Great Person improvement (Academy, Manufactory, Customs house, Landmark, Holy site, Citadel).
Many technologies have an Insight: do something related (build 2 Mines, meet another civilization, defeat a unit…) and that technology becomes 33% cheaper to research.

Each Insight works once and is checked at the start of every turn, only for technologies you haven't researched yet. A popup tells you when you earn one. You can earn an Insight long before you research its technology: the discount waits for you and shows in the research cost. Note: while you research a technology that has an Insight, the technology screen shows every other technology with the same discount. Select one to see its real cost; the research itself is always correct.

Almost every technology has an Insight. Technologies cost 33% more to make up for it: with about three quarters of the Insights you research at the usual speed, with all of them a bit faster, and with none much slower.
Banked Insights (earned, technology not researched yet) are listed in your capital's buildings as "Insight: <technology>". They disappear when you research the technology.
When you found your first city, and every time you enter a new era, you choose one of three Legacies: permanent bonuses that shape your civilization (military, economy or culture/science).

Legacies appear as special buildings in your capital and move with it. If you are more than 2 technologies behind the other civilizations' average, a fourth option appears: Rising Star, a free technology.

War Weariness (top bar) grows while you are at war with major civilizations, when you declare war, lose units, and conquer or lose cities. Every 5 points add +5% unhappiness from population, up to +50%.
At peace it falls each turn, and ending a war halves it. Honor, the Aztecs, the Great Bath, the Pax Dei belief and the Total Mobilization Legacy help you recover faster.

When you declare war, choose a Casus Belli: War Fervor (veteran recruits) or Blitz (+1 Movement), each +2 War Weariness, or pay for Propaganda (-5 War Weariness). When someone declares war on you, Call to Arms (Mobilization) speeds up military production. When a war ends, Reconstruction boosts production for a while. If you lose a city, you can Rally the Nation.
Imperial Strain (top bar) counts how many cities you have beyond 125% of what the other civilizations average, with one city free.

Each point makes technologies 4% and policies 5% more expensive, and adds 10% unhappiness from the number of cities. A bigger empire is still stronger, just with diminishing returns. Rome tolerates Strain better than others.

Natural wonders are worth settling for. Their tile yields even without a citizen working it, each natural wonder tile you own gives +2 Happiness, and Quarters next to one get +2 of their yield (Academy: Science, Market: Gold, Artisan: Production, Sacred Grove: Faith).
The first time you see one, an Expedition lets you choose: Survey (Science), Pilgrimage (Faith and Culture) or Tall Tales (Gold). Amounts double from the Renaissance on.
Each natural wonder also has a signature effect. Most grant a permanent promotion to any unit, of any civilization, that moves next to them (like the Fountain of Youth's Rejuvenation):
Fountain of Youth: Rejuvenation, all healing doubled (military land units)
Mount Sinai: Revelation, +50% XP from combat (military units)
Mount Kailash: Altitude Training, double movement and +10% Strength in Hills (military land units)
Rock of Gibraltar: Pillars of Hercules, +1 Movement (military naval units)
Grand Mesa: Vantage, +1 Sight (land units)
Mount Fuji: Spirit of Fuji, no strength penalty when wounded (military land units)
Barringer Crater: Star Metal, +10% Strength (melee land units)
Uluru: Songlines, ignores Zone of Control (military land units)
Sri Pada: Pilgrim's Path, +1 Movement (civilian units)
The others act on their surroundings or their owner:
Great Barrier Reef: any unit that ends its turn next to it, even yours, takes 20 damage
Krakatoa: enemy units that end their turn next to it, inside the borders of a civilization at war with them, take 30 damage
Old Faithful: units that end their turn next to it heal 20 HP, even after moving or fighting
Cerro de Potosi: while you own it, all your Mines yield +1 Gold
El Dorado: 500 Gold to the first civilization to discover it
When your empire falls to -5 Happiness or worse, Unrest breaks out (at most once every 15 turns, scaled by game speed). Choose how to answer:
• Martial Law: for 10 turns, +2 Happiness in every city with a military unit inside, -10% Production everywhere, and no rebels.
• Concessions: pay 15 Gold per city for +1 Happiness in every city for 10 turns.
• Ignore them: free, but half the time a band of rebels rises near your capital.
Unrest is a warning: below -10 Happiness cities stop growing, produce 50% less and fight worse, and below -20 rebels appear on their own.
Battering Rams and Siege Towers give adjacent melee units +30%/+40% Strength against cities. Field Medics heal adjacent units. They are civilians: enemies can capture them, so keep them escorted.
A unit that loses 50 or more HP in a single attack becomes Shaken (-15% Strength for a turn). A unit that defeats an enemy becomes Emboldened (+10% Strength for 2 turns).
Mercenary Companies can only be bought with Gold, never trained, and cost more upkeep.
